title_guess: Bank nationalisation in India: RBI 1949, SBI 1955, 14 banks in 1969, crisis and the Narasimham committees
recurring_cast: blue horizontal timeline with year ticks (one long timeline that pans and zooms)
green law sheet icon dropped on the year of each Act
national emblem placed above an institution to mean 'state-owned'
committee icon: five suited people behind a desk banner, chair coloured red
coloured era bands on the timeline (blue = nationalisation era, red = crisis era)
running_examples: 1969 Act: 14 banks nationalised, about 85% of banking business
seven SBI associate banks drawn as seven bank buildings
one timeline carried through the whole video: 1947 → 1980 nationalisation era → crisis → 1991 LPG

best_moments.why: a yellow 'nationalised' zone grows over the timeline and everything inside it (RBI, SBI, seven associate banks) reads as state-owned: ownership as a region
the era band turns from blue to red after 1980: one colour change shows a calm policy era giving way to crisis
committees drawn as a row of people at a desk, one above and one below the line with Roman I and II: two committees told apart at a glance
a dotted 'part of' elbow arrow plugs financial sector reforms into the 1991 LPG package: nesting without a tree
clearing back to the bare timeline gives a one-glance recap of 1947-1991 before the next-topic question mark

weak_moments.why: 30 s of paragraph text on private banks neglecting farms and small industry; nothing drawn
'14 banks' and '85%' only in a text note; no 14 buildings or filling share
'banking sector 100% nationalised' is the video's wording and is not accurate (private and foreign banks remained); BIE must not copy it
aims of nationalisation as a ticked text list for about 30 s
about 70 s of before/after text boxes on the government's role

segments.teaches: recap: RBI was nationalised in 1949 under a 1948 Act; the Imperial Bank became the State Bank of India in 1955 and was nationalised

elements.what: blue line with ticks 1947, 1948, 1949, 1955
Indian flag on a pole at 1947
green law sheet at 1948 with a stalk down to the Act name
RBI coin emblem at 1949
national emblem on a stalk above the RBI coin with the word 'nationalised'
small yellow 'NATIONALISED' card at 1955 holding the national emblem and SBI mark
old bank name struck through, State Bank of India written under it

segments.notes: Fast recap (built in about 15 s) of the previous video's ending; E36 ends on this same canvas. Ownership is marked by putting the national emblem above an institution. [Events: 4 add, 0 big/reset in 16 s, about one change every 4 s.]
segments.idea: Before 1969 the state already owned the RBI (1949) and the SBI (1955).
segments.shown_as: a blue timeline runs left to right; a flag plants at 1947, a law sheet drops at 1948, the RBI coin sits at 1949 with the national emblem raised above it on a stalk to mean 'now state-owned'; at 1955 a small yellow 'nationalised' card holds the emblem and the SBI mark, and under it the old bank name is struck through and the new one written below

segments.teaches: the 'nationalised' zone grows to cover RBI, SBI and, after the 1959 SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act, seven associate banks

elements.what: yellow 'NATIONALISED' band grows from the 1955 card to span 1949-1959, with a large national emblem at its top
law sheets under 1955 and 1959 with Act names
small bank buildings in two rows (4 + 3) inside the yellow band

segments.notes: Strong idea: a coloured zone over a span of the timeline = 'under state ownership'; members are placed inside it. [Events: 3 add, 1 big/reset in 24 s, about one change every 6 s.]
segments.idea: By 1959 the RBI, the SBI and SBI's seven associate banks were all in state hands.
segments.shown_as: the small 'nationalised' card stretches into a wide yellow zone over the timeline from 1949 to 1959 under one large national emblem; the RBI coin and SBI mark now sit inside it, a law sheet drops at 1959, and seven small bank buildings pop into the zone in two rows - everything inside the zone is state-owned
segments.example: seven associate banks of SBI drawn as seven bank buildings

segments.teaches: even after this, most banking was private, and private banks neglected agriculture and small industry as risky and unprofitable

elements.what: light-blue box beside the yellow zone: most of banking still private
black underline under 'private sector banks'
paragraph hanging from the underline on a stalk: farms and small industry neglected as risky

segments.notes: 30 s of paragraph text. The neglected sectors (farmer, small workshop) could have been drawn turning away from a private bank. [Events: 7 add, 0 big/reset in 32 s, about one change every 5 s.]
segments.idea: Private banks still held most of banking and avoided lending to farmers and small industry, which made the case for 1969.
segments.shown_as: a light-blue text box appears beside the yellow state zone; its last words are underlined in black and a stalk drops from the underline to a paragraph naming the neglected sectors - no farmer, factory or loan is drawn

segments.teaches: the 1969 Banking Nationalisation Act took over 14 banks holding about 85% of banking business; a further acquisition Act came in 1980

elements.what: law sheet at 1969 with a stalk down to the Act name
magenta note: 14 banks, about 85% of business (85% in bold)
law sheet at 1980 with the long acquisition-and-transfer Act name above it

segments.notes: The text boxes of the previous segment are removed first. Missed chance: 14 bank buildings could have walked into the yellow zone, or an 85% share could have filled. [Events: 5 add, 2 big/reset in 31 s, about one change every 4 s.]
segments.idea: In 1969 the state took over 14 big banks (about 85% of banking); in 1980 another Act extended this.
segments.shown_as: the text boxes vanish; the timeline runs on past the yellow zone; a law sheet drops at 1969 with a stalk down to the Act name and a magenta note giving '14 banks' and '85%'; a second law sheet drops at 1980 with its Act name above - the 14 banks themselves are not drawn
segments.example: 14 banks nationalised in 1969 = about 85% of banking business

segments.teaches: 1947-1980 was the nationalisation era; its aims were financial inclusion, rural reach, credit to priority sectors (agriculture, small industry) and growth of deposits and household savings

elements.what: detail replaced by one thick blue band labelled NATIONALIZATION from 1947 (flag) to 1980
magenta stalk at 1980: banking sector fully nationalised (video's claim)
four aims, each with a green tick box

segments.notes: Era band = a whole policy period compressed into one coloured bar (reusable for history). The '100% nationalised' wording is the video's claim and is not accurate. Aims are a ticked text list. [Events: 6 add, 1 big/reset in 45 s, about one change every 6 s.]
segments.idea: Nationalisation (1947-1980) aimed to bring banking to everyone: rural branches, priority-sector credit, more deposits and savings.
segments.shown_as: the crowded timeline is swapped for a clean one where 1947-1980 becomes a single thick blue era band titled 'nationalization'; a stalk at 1980 says the sector is fully state-owned; four green-ticked aims write on one by one under the band

segments.teaches: in the late 1980s and early 1990s India hit an economic crisis: high inflation, large fiscal deficits, a balance of payments crisis and a stagnant economy

elements.what: view slides left; a red band continues after 1980 labelled late 1980s-early 1990s and ECONOMIC CRISIS
four red-square symptoms hanging on a stalk below the red band

segments.notes: Colour code: blue band = calm policy era, red band = crisis era. Symptoms are text only (no rising price tag, no empty treasury). [Events: 6 add, 1 big/reset in 24 s, about one change every 3 s.]
segments.idea: After the nationalisation era came a crisis period with high inflation, deficits and a payments crisis.
segments.shown_as: the timeline slides left; after 1980 the band turns from blue to red - a 'crisis' era - and four red-square symptoms hang below it on a stalk

segments.teaches: in 1991 the Narasimham Committee on the Financial System was set up; in 1998 a second Narasimham committee on banking sector reforms

elements.what: red elbow arrow climbing from 1991 to the committee
committee: five suited people behind a dark desk banner, the middle one red as chair
chair's name on a stalk above each committee
red down arrow from 1998 to the second committee below the line
Roman numerals I and II marking the two committees

segments.notes: Committee drawn as a row of people at a desk with the chair highlighted: a reusable 'committee / commission' icon. One above and one below the line separates the two. [Events: 6 add, 0 big/reset in 49 s, about one change every 8 s.]
segments.idea: Two expert committees (1991 and 1998), both chaired by Narasimham, shaped banking reform.
segments.shown_as: a red elbow arrow climbs from 1991 to a row of five suited figures at a desk - a committee, its chair coloured red and named on a stalk; at 1998 a red arrow drops to a second, identical committee below the line; Roman I and II tags tell the two apart

segments.teaches: the first Narasimham committee examined every part of the financial system (capital market, money market, insurance, payments, regulation, banking, NBFCs) and recommended reform and modernisation; the system was restructured on its advice

elements.what: committee row (five suited people at a desk)
arrow labelled 'examine' from committee to the list
green 'all aspects of' chip over the heading
seven parts of the financial system with green squares
recommendation card with a document-and-tick icon under the committee
blue highlight on the 'banking sector' line
blue note under a rule: system restructured on committee I's advice

segments.notes: The 'examine' arrow plus a list is a simple scope diagram; highlighting one list item narrows the story to banks without a camera move. [Events: 4 add, 1 big/reset in 31 s, about one change every 6 s.]
segments.idea: The 1991 committee looked at the whole financial system and recommended reforms; banking was one part of it.
segments.shown_as: the committee sends a labelled 'examine' arrow to a list of seven parts of the financial system; a recommendation document card pops in under the committee; then the 'banking sector' line lights up blue to narrow the story to banks

segments.teaches: the committee's recommendations became financial sector reforms, which were part of the 1991 LPG (liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation) reforms

elements.what: document-with-tick icon beside the chair's name, dotted down arrow to 'financial sector reforms'
black underline under 1991
angled stalk from 1991 to 'LPG reforms' with the three words in brackets
dotted elbow arrow labelled 'part of' from financial sector reforms into LPG
new blue band begins after 1991

segments.notes: 'Part of' dotted connector shows nesting (a smaller reform inside a bigger package) without drawing a tree. [Events: 10 add, 1 big/reset in 41 s, about one change every 4 s.]
segments.idea: The committee's advice turned into financial sector reforms, one piece of the 1991 LPG reforms.
segments.shown_as: the view returns to the full timeline; a document-with-tick icon beside the committee drops a dotted arrow to 'financial sector reforms'; 1991 is underlined and an angled stalk leads to 'LPG reforms'; a dotted elbow arrow marked 'part of' plugs the financial reforms into LPG, and a new blue band starts after 1991

segments.teaches: 1991 changed the government's role: before, the state nationalised key industries, directed economic activity and limited the private sector; after, it moved to a market-oriented approach with more private participation

elements.what: black headline box at 1991: role of government transformed (shown briefly)
dotted vertical line dropping from 1991, splitting the lower canvas
pink 'before' boxes on the left
light-blue 'after' boxes on the right

segments.notes: About 70 s of reading. The dotted line from a year splitting before/after is a good reusable layout; the content could be pictures (state hand holding the factories vs open market stalls). [Events: 9 add, 1 big/reset in 71 s, about one change every 7 s.]
segments.idea: 1991 is the turning point from a state-led economy to a market-led one.
segments.shown_as: a black headline box pops at 1991, then a dotted vertical line drops from 1991 and splits the lower canvas: three pink boxes stack on the 'before' side (left), two light-blue boxes on the 'after' side (right) - side and colour carry before/after, the content is all sentences

segments.teaches: recap of the whole timeline and teaser: banking sector reforms after 1991 come next
